finding_resolutions.explanation: Confirmed against GDD Section 2 (Victory/input-shutdown ownership) and Section 4 (Final escape/victory coordination): Player Movement is explicitly named as an owner-controlled suspend/re-enable interface provider, symmetric with Fireball/Frost Field/Force Wave, but the candidate's player-movement item had no gdd_evidence or acceptance criterion for it. Added a matching gdd_evidence row, an owner-side acceptance criterion, and a mirrored validation requirement to player-movement. final-escape-victory's existing consumption criterion and its dependency on player-movement were left unchanged as instructed.

This deterministic finding flags the same PC-07 requirement (Player Movement owner-controlled suspend/re-enable interface) as unrepresented. Classified per the requirement-representation repair policy: this is behavior/constraint owned by an existing implementation item (player-movement), not a distinct executable responsibility, so it is represented as an acceptance criterion (plus matching gdd_evidence and validation_requirements) on player-movement rather than as a new work item, resolving the same coverage gap as PC-F1.

result.reasoning: Both supplied findings identify the same underlying gap: the GDD's Section 2 "Victory/input-shutdown ownership" bullet and Section 4 "Final escape/victory coordination" invariant explicitly name Player Movement as one of five owners (alongside Door/Interaction, Fireball, Frost Field, Force Wave) that must expose an owner-controlled gameplay-enable/suspend interface. Verified this against Docs/GDD/No_Safe_Circle_GDD.md lines 100 and 214, and confirmed via the original candidate that Fireball, Frost Field, and Force Wave each already carry a matching gdd_evidence + acceptance criterion (e.g. fireball at original lines 503-506), while player-movement's four acceptance criteria (mouse-directed movement, pointer target, movement-restriction interface, reset entry point) omitted this fifth required capability. Per the requirement-representation repair policy, this is a behavior/constraint owned by an existing implementation item, not a distinct organizational/executable responsibility, so no new work item is warranted -- it belongs as an acceptance criterion (plus gdd_evidence) on player-movement, with a mirrored validation requirement analogous to final-escape-victory's owner-side Play Mode check. This single correction resolves both the agent-sourced finding (PC-F1) and the deterministic coverage finding (PC-07), which describe the identical gap. final-escape-victory's existing consumer-side acceptance criterion and its depends_on edge to player-movement were left untouched per the finding's explicit instruction not to remove them. No other candidate fields were touched, and no verification/reconciliation output paths were added to sources.
